relations.evidence: The maximum number of cursor-aware Eventing functions that can coexist on a given source keyspace. notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badge anywhere on this REST reference - every gate is either the classic RBAC role pair (Full Admin/Eventing Full Admin, for Global scope) or 'any authorized user' with function-scope access (for Scoped), consistent with this batch's other RBAC findings. Separately, a genuine internal inconsistency: the 'Modify Service Config' endpoint's own primary examples use `http://$ADMIN:$PASSWORD@$HOST:8096/api/v1/config`, but its 'Allow/Disallow interbucket recursion' examples immediately below use a differently-shaped URL for what appears to be the SAME config endpoint - `http://$HOST:8091/_p/event/api/v1/config` (port 8091, not 8096; path prefixed with `/_p/event/`, not bare `/api/v1/`; credentials passed via curl's `-u` flag rather than embedded in the URL). The page does not explain whether these are two genuinely different endpoints, an older undocumented path retained for compatibility, or an editorial inconsistency.

cross_component_finding: This page's Function Settings schema (settings_schema, ~35 fields) is the authoritative internal-field-name specification behind almost every UI-display-label setting this batch's other pages describe only by name: eventing-lifecycle.json's Settings table (System Log Level=log_level, Script Timeout=execution_timeout, OnDeploy Timeout=on_deploy_timeout, Timer Context Max Size=timer_context_size, Workers=worker_count, Language compatibility=language_compatibility), eventing-faq.json's lcb_retry_count, and eventing-function-export.json's sample JSON fields. Reading this page after those closes every open 'what is the internal name for X' question this batch's other pages left implicit. It also surfaces several fields no other page in this batch names at all: cpp_worker_thread_count, cursor_checkpoint_timeout, lcb_inst_capacity, lcb_timeout, num_timer_partitions, sock_batch_size, tick_duration, handler_headers/handler_footers, bucket_cache_size/bucket_cache_age, curl_max_allowed_resp_size, allow_transaction_mutations, high_seq_check_interval, max_unacked_bytes/max_unacked_count, max_parallel_vb.
cross_product_finding: This entire page - Basic-auth REST endpoints on ports 8096/18096, bound to a per-node Eventing REST service, with a Global/Scoped/Unscoped security model keyed to the classic RBAC role catalogue and to a bucket.scope Function Scope - has no equivalent anywhere in the corpus's cloud/ tree. This batch's own eventing-rbac.json (Capella twin, already extracted) documents a completely different access surface for the same underlying capability: Capella gates Eventing purely through (1) Capella UI project roles (Data Reader/Data Writer/Project Owner) and (2) the cluster-access-credential-type Basic/Advanced axis, with a single bundled privilege (privilege:capella-advanced-access-eventing-manage, always paired with Data Read) - not a Function-scoped HTTP Basic-auth catalogue of dozens of named endpoints with per-endpoint Global/Scoped/Unscoped rules. Capella's management plane instead exposes its own, separately-documented capella:management-api. Two further settings on this page make the platform-management difference concrete rather than just structural: num_nodes_running (new in 8.0, letting a Server administrator pin a Function's scope to run on a chosen SUBSET of the cluster's own Eventing nodes) and ram_quota/cursor_limit/enable_debugger as directly-settable Service Config fields - all node-topology-aware controls that presuppose the caller can see and address individual nodes, which is exactly the kind of control a managed multi-tenant service does not hand to its customers. This is the clearest, most concrete evidence in the whole batch for why this page - and its sibling eventing-debugging-and-diagnosability.json - have no Capella twin: not because the underlying capability is absent from Capella (this batch already found the live debugger described in Capella's own Terminologies glossary), but because the ADMINISTRATIVE SURFACE for controlling it at the node level is structurally Server-only.
